relations.subject: service:eventing-service
relations.evidence:
Is Eventing an MDS-enabled service?  
Yes. MDS enables workload isolation in a Couchbase cluster. Eventing nodes can be added as more Functions are added, or if the mutation rates are high.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate, applied to a newly-minted object
relations.evidence: Eventing retries transient and recoverable errors every 200 ms (5 times per second) until the function reaches its script timeout (60 seconds by default). When you configure the `lcb_retry_count` in the [Eventing function settings](../eventing-rest-api/index.md#settings%5Fschema), with a non-zero value, Eventing limits retries to the specified count. After Eventing exhausts the configured retries, it throws an exception for that operation.

relations.subject: eventing:lcb-retry-count-setting
relations.evidence: When you configure the `lcb_retry_count` in the [Eventing function settings](../eventing-rest-api/index.md#settings%5Fschema), with a non-zero value, Eventing limits retries to the specified count.

relations.object: ~2 MB fixed space per Function (1024 docs x 1884 bytes)
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: Each Eventing function always requires a fixed amount of space of about 2MB (1024 docs \* 1884 bytes).

relations.subject: eventing:timer
relations.object: ~0.2 MB additional space per Function using timers before 6.6.1; ~0.04 MB from 6.6.1 on
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: If an Eventing function uses timers, then an additional fixed amount of space of about 0.2MB (1024 \* docs of 196 bytes) is needed. From version 6.6.1 on only 0.04MB (256 docs \* 196 bytes) is needed if the function uses timers.

relations.subject: eventing:rebalance-operation
relations.evidence: Due to a regression, [MB-43343](https://issues.couchbase.com/browse/MB-43343), impacting only 6.6.1 during a rebalance in of an Eventing node a race can occur resulting in Eventing functions becoming hung in deploying state.

relations.subject: service:eventing-service
relations.object: 256 MB default; raising to 512 MB typically resolves a >48-worker stall
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: This is typically related to resources given to the Eventing service and can be solved by adding additional Memory Quota to Eventing in the Cluster Settings. By default Eventing allocates 256 MB, raising this value to 512 MB will typically solve this resource issue (this is one of the rare instances that you may need to raise the Memory Quota for Eventing).

relations.evidence: Yes, node-to-node encryption is available in the Couchbase Server for the Eventing Service in the 7.X train starting with version 7.0.2 and the 6.X train starting with version 6.6.5\.

relations.subject: eventing:function
relations.object: temporary pause during a node-to-node encryption toggle
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted; object is a literal
relations.evidence: When node-to-node encryption is enabled or disabled all deployed Eventing Functions need to be temporarily paused and can be resumed after the necessary changes have been made (to prevents the potential loss of mutations during the encryption change.)

notable_absence.finding: As on the Capella twin, this - the longest page in the batch - names no Capella role/privilege and, in fact, no Server RBAC role either: every question is architectural or operational, never an access-control question. Separately: 'How to invoke a REST endpoint from inside the Function?' links to an absolute, hardcoded external URL - https://docs.couchbase.com/server/6.5/eventing/eventing-api.html - rather than to this same batch's own eventing-rest-api/index.md, which documents the current 8.0 REST API. An 8.0-current page pointing its reader to a 6.5 archived doc for its own REST API is a stale-link anomaly worth flagging, though extraction does not correct it.

cross_component_finding: This page directly corroborates, on its own primary topic page, the cross-page finding this batch's eventing-memory-quota.json could only support via evidence_source: the exact same 256 MB default / 512 MB remediation sentence appears here as first-class, on-page evidence. It also corroborates eventing-lifecycle.json's mutual-exclusion finding (deploy/undeploy/pause/resume/delete vs. rebalance) with an added specific regression citation (MB-43343, 6.6.1-only), and independently states the same 832-1856-byte per-active-timer space cost already recorded with full context in eventing-timers.json, this time attributing the number to a slightly different breakdown (root/alarm/context, 'up to three documents... sometimes only two').
cross_product_finding: Node-to-node encryption for the Eventing Service specifically lags the rest of Couchbase Server's services by version: 'on earlier versions (in either train), when _all_ is specified, the data passed to and from all other Couchbase Services is passed in encrypted form, whereas the data passed to and from the Eventing Service continues to be passed in _unencrypted_ form.' No Capella twin exists for this FAQ's exact wording to compare against (the memory-quota question is Capella's own byte-identical FAQ entry, already used in eventing-memory-quota.json), so whether this same lag applied to, or was ever visible on, Capella clusters running the equivalent pre-7.0.2/6.6.5 server versions is not something either tree's docs state.
